correctness.rationale: A positive selfadjoint generalized Jacobi operator has host essential band \([\kappa,\kappa+4]\). Its square-summable external-band solutions are necessarily symmetric geometric tails, and the matching function has strictly negative derivative on both allowable decay-root branches; this excludes all other point spectrum and justifies simple roots and strict edge boundaries. Subtraction of the two exact defect equations forces \(\mu=2pq/(1+pq)\), and back substitution yields the displayed \(\kappa_0\); physical positivity is exactly the strict inequality. Conversely the reconstructed parameters make both square-summable modes satisfy every site equation. Fixed-seed checker: 1,600 random forward/case count checks, 337 successful two-mode reconstructions, eight independent 601-site eigenvalue comparisons, 98 feasible-input sign probes; numeric evidence is not a substitute for the proof. Finite-matrix comparison examples have decay factors of magnitude below 0.82, so truncation effects are negligible at the stated numerical tolerance.

originality.rationale: The reviewed claim is the sharp inverse feasible set and uniqueness from two frequencies, NOT the known two-sided existence of impurity modes. Manzhelii–Feodosyev (2025) supplies a more general forward three-parameter dispersion treatment that covers the presence of both modes, and Ramakrishnan–Matlack (2024) includes a finite grounded-chain two-mode phenomenon. Tian–Li (2013) and Tian–Dai (2006) solve finite-chain inverse problems with two eigenpairs and extra known physical parameters. The reverse image/positivity theorem from only two eigenvalues was not found in inspected accessible main texts or bounded published-results search. Exact prior implicit or unavailable treatment remains a specifically documented risk.
residual_risks: arXiv:2505.24497 contains the same model within its general three-parameter forward formulas; the new inverse theorem might be a short unrecorded algebraic corollary, and forward novelty is expressly disclaimed.
The complete 2013 Tian–Li grounded inverse paper and 1962 Takeno et al. impurity paper were not accessible for full-text inspection; only problem/abstract material was compared.
Semantic database retrieval and finite source coverage do not establish independent scientific priority; additional non-indexed inverse work is possible.

value.rationale: A natural inverse-defect diagnostic has exactly two unknown material properties (local mass and substrate pinning), while experiments could return the two isolated frequencies without resolving their complete eigenvectors. The theorem identifies the exact joint feasible observation region, reconstructs both physical parameters without fitting or arbitrary choices and excludes spectrally inconsistent measurements. The strict boundary is mathematically meaningful because it coincides with the zero-local-pinning limit. This is a complete physical inverse classification in an established lattice model, not a mere tabulated finite case or the already known forward localization phenomenon. Noise and finite-size stability remain unproved.
